analysis: The only change in this PR is in the test helper provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Helpers/MockCoordinator.swift. It adds pushPrefetchModel(modelId:priority:) at head lines 460-462, which sends CoordinatorMessage.prefetchModel through the existing sendCoordinatorMessage path. The mock binds only to 127.0.0.1 and exists only in the test target. It adds no production route, no deployed attack surface, and no new authorization or encryption behavior. The helper does not touch keys, attestation, prefix-cache storage (T-041), or provider tokens (A-008). The call relies on a CoordinatorMessage.prefetchModel case and its initializer (modelId, priority). Those are outside the supplied evidence, but the mock already handled the provider's prefetchModelStatus message, which makes it likely the case exists in ProviderProtocolCodec. If the case is missing, the result is a compile failure, not a security issue. The prefetch handler in the provider is not in this batch. A later pass could check that the production handler authenticates the model ID against the catalog and weight hash. That would be an existing concern, not something this PR introduces. I found no security regression.
